source.title: [software-development-practices:nist-ssdf] github/gh-aw-firewall repository guidance
source.body:
Repository-observable SSDF controls for `github/gh-aw-firewall` are generally strong at commit `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab`: pinned GitHub Actions, scheduled CodeQL/dependency/supply-chain scans, SBOM/cosign coverage for container images, and regression-oriented test gates are all present. The main evidence-backed gap is release integrity for non-container CLI assets: I found checksum validation for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, but not a repo-observable signature or provenance verification path for those assets themselves. This review is advisory and non-binding; it does not prove security, compliance, certification, endorsement, or SSDF conformance. **Action:** Maintainer should assign this issue to Copilot to add signed or attested verification for CLI release assets and update installer/docs; accept when a release publishes verifiable signatures or provenance for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, `install.sh` or setup paths validate them, and release documentation shows the verification flow. - Critical finding: container release integrity is stronger than CLI release integrity today (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `docs/image-verification.md`, `install.sh`, `docs/releasing.md`). - Critical finding: repository-observable detection and prevention controls are broad and active in source (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, `.github/dependabot.yml`). - Critical metric: 1 promoted backlog item met the threshold for an evidence-backed repository change in this run.
Agent prompt Implement a release-integrity improvement for `github/gh-aw-firewall` focused on SSDF PS.2.1 / PS.3.1 / PS.3.2. Requirements: 1. Extend the release pipeline so `awf-linux-x64`, `awf-linux-arm64`, `awf-darwin-x64`, `awf-darwin-arm64`, `awf-bundle.js`, and `awf.tgz` ship with verifiable signatures or provenance that is generated in CI and published with the release. 2. Update `install.sh` and any setup/install path that currently trusts only `checksums.txt` so it validates the new signature/provenance material before installation, while still failing closed on mismatches. 3. Update release/install docs to show how users verify the CLI assets, parallel to the existing container-image verification guidance. 4. Add or update focused tests that cover failure paths for tampered assets/metadata. 5. Keep existing container signing/SBOM behavior intact. Deliverables: - Workflow changes in `.github/workflows/release.yml` - Installer/setup changes (`install.sh`, `action.yml`, or both as needed) - Documentation updates (`docs/releasing.md`, `README.md`, `docs/image-verification.md` or a better-named CLI verification doc) - Tests proving the verification path fails closed
Assessment metadata, scope, and limitations ### Metadata - Target repository: `github/gh-aw-firewall` - Analyzed commit: `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab` - Target snapshot source: local `target/` checkout plus bounded GitHub metadata reads - Source verification date: `2026-10-13` - Final SSDF baseline used: `NIST SP 800-218 Version 1.1 (final, February 2022)` - Official URLs: - `https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/ssdf` - `https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final` - `https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-218` - Machine-readable marker: - `` ### Scope and assumptions - Repository-observable review only: committed files in `target/` and bounded accessible GitHub metadata. - Assessed against the current final SSDF baseline above. The NIST SSDF project page also references `SP 800-218A` as a final SSDF community profile for generative AI and dual-use foundation models, but it augments `SP 800-218` and was **not** treated as a replacement baseline for this repository review. - Findings are risk-based and scoped to evidence visible in this repository snapshot; absence of repository evidence is **not** proof that an organizational control does not exist. ### Inaccessible or non-repository evidence - Branch protection / rulesets details were not readable with the available credential (`gh api repos/github/gh-aw-firewall/branches/main/protection` returned `403 Resource not accessible by personal access token`). - GitHub security feature state, private security alerts, secret-scanning alerts, advisories, internal training records, personnel/process evidence, and private incident-response artifacts were not assessed. - Workflow files provide evidence of intended controls, but this run did not establish historical execution success for every workflow.
PO / PS / PW / RV practice-to-evidence matrix ### Practice matrix | Practice / task focus | Status | Repository-observable evidence | Evidence limits / assumptions | Concrete improvement and risk reduced | |---|---|---|---|---| | `PO.1.1`-`PO.1.3` — define and communicate software-development security requirements | `PARTIAL` | `docs/security.md` defines disclosure expectations; `docs/awf-config-spec.md`, `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, and `docs/image-verification.md` document security-relevant product and release requirements; `README.md` surfaces supported security behaviors. | No visible organization-wide policy register, annual review record, or third-party acquisition/security-contract evidence. | Consolidate repository-scoped secure-release requirements for CLI and container artifacts in one maintained policy/doc so release obligations do not drift. Reduces missed integrity requirements. | | `PO.2.1`-`PO.2.3` — roles, responsibilities, training, leadership commitment | `HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns a maintainer; `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/security.md` define contributor/security reporting paths. | Training, management commitment, and role review cadence are not repository-observable. | Maintain explicit code ownership and review paths; confirm separately whether secure-development roles and training are formalized. Reduces reliance on implicit ownership. | | `PO.3.1`-`PO.3.3` — supporting toolchains and artifacts | `OBSERVED` | `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, and `release.yml` codify automated checks; actions are commit-pinned; release artifacts include `checksums.txt`, `containers.txt`, and schemas. | Runtime hardening and monitoring of hosted CI infrastructure itself are not directly visible. | Preserve pinned-action and artifact-producing workflows; add equivalent provenance coverage for CLI assets. Reduces toolchain tampering blind spots. | | `PO.4.1`-`PO.4.2` — criteria for security checks and protected evidence | `PARTIAL` | High/critical dependency findings fail in `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml`; PR-built container CVEs fail in `supply-chain-scan.yml`; coverage regressions fail in `test-coverage.yml`; CodeQL runs on push/PR/schedule. | Criteria exist across workflows, but I did not find one central repo doc that ties gates, exceptions, and approval criteria together. | Keep machine-enforced thresholds close to the workflows and document exceptions centrally when they are allowed. Reduces inconsistent triage. | | `PO.5.1`-`PO.5.2` — secure development environments and hardened endpoints | `PARTIAL` | `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, `docs/security.md`, and product docs describe isolated execution, deny-by-default egress, and credential isolation patterns; several workflows use `persist-credentials: false` and least-privilege `permissions`. | Developer endpoint hardening, MFA, runner segmentation, and operational monitoring evidence are mostly outside the repository. | Continue isolating credentials and minimizing runner permissions; verify separately that endpoint and runner hardening matches the documented model. Reduces environment compromise exposure. | | `PS.1.1` — protect code and configuration from unauthorized access/tampering | `PARTIAL` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` exists; workflow actions are SHA-pinned; repository uses GitHub workflow files and code review paths typical for controlled changes. | Repository ACLs, branch protection, and mandatory review enforcement could not be confirmed with the available credential. | Verify rulesets/branch protection separately and keep CODEOWNERS current. Reduces unreviewed change risk. | | `PS.2.1` — provide a mechanism to verify software release integrity | `GAP_FOUND` | `docs/image-verification.md` documents cosign verification for container images. `install.sh` and release docs validate CLI assets with `checksums.txt`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` generates that checksum file, but I did not find repo-observable signatures or provenance verification for `awf-*` binaries or `awf.tgz`. | There could be external verification material not visible here, but none was referenced in repository docs, workflows, or installer paths reviewed. | Publish and validate signed or attested verification material for CLI release assets. Reduces risk that a tampered binary and matching checksum on the same release channel evade detection. | | `PS.3.1`-`PS.3.2` — archive releases and maintain/share provenance | `PARTIAL` | `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes binaries, tarballs, schemas, `checksums.txt`, and `containers.txt`; container images are signed and SBOM-attested; some enclave/cloud-hypervisor artifacts include provenance files. | Equivalent provenance/signature coverage for all CLI assets was not found. Long-term archive controls beyond GitHub Releases are not visible. | Extend provenance/signature publication from selected artifacts to the CLI release set. Reduces incomplete release-forensics coverage. | | `PW.1.1`-`PW.1.3` — design to meet security requirements and mitigate risks | `OBSERVED` | `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/authentication-architecture.md`, `docs/sandbox-design.md`, and `docs/enclaves-architecture.md` capture security architecture and threat-model reasoning. | This does not prove that every change receives formal threat modeling. | Preserve design docs and keep threat-model updates coupled to security-relevant changes. Reduces design drift. | | `PW.2.1` — independent review of design against security requirements/risk | `PARTIAL` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` supports review; `.github/workflows/security-review.md` exists as a dedicated threat-model/security review workflow; release/process docs contain review-oriented checks. | Could not confirm mandatory execution or independence for every design-affecting change. | Define when security design review is required and link resulting artifacts to changes. Reduces missed design regressions. | | `PW.4.1` / `PW.4.2` / `PW.4.4` — acquire, maintain, and verify reused software/components | `OBSERVED` | `.github/dependabot.yml` updates npm, Docker, and GitHub Actions dependencies; `dependency-audit.yml` and `supply-chain-scan.yml` verify dependency risk; `package-lock.json` and `docs-site/package-lock.json` lock dependencies. | Supplier assurance outside what is codified in repo tooling is not visible. | Keep automated update + audit loops in place and include new ecosystems as they are added. Reduces stale dependency exposure. | | `PW.5.1` — secure coding practices | `OBSERVED` | `package.json` includes `eslint-plugin-security`; source contains dedicated lint/test rules (for example `eslint-rules/no-unsafe-execa.js`); `codeql.yml` enables `security-extended,security-and-quality`. | Secure-coding training and review quality are not directly observable. | Preserve secure-coding automation and add targeted rules when new risk classes emerge. Reduces recurring implementation flaws. | | `PW.6.1`-`PW.6.2` — hardened compilation/interpreter/build configuration | `OBSERVED` | `release.yml` pins actions, signs container images with cosign, generates SBOMs, disables cache for security-critical agent image builds, and runs seccomp verification checks for agent images. | Build-host hardening and provenance for all non-container binaries were not fully visible. | Extend hardened-build outputs with CLI-asset provenance/signatures. Reduces build artifact substitution risk. | | `PW.7.1`-`PW.7.2` — review/analyze human-readable code | `PARTIAL` | `codeql.yml`, ESLint security rules, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and numerous tests provide automated/static review layers. | Mandatory human review enforcement could not be confirmed via rulesets/branch protection. | Keep static analysis current and validate human-review enforcement separately. Reduces code-level vulnerability escape. | | `PW.8.1`-`PW.8.2` — test executable code and record findings | `OBSERVED` | `test-coverage.yml`, `build-test.md`, smoke/test workflows, integration/unit tests in `package.json`, and security-focused scan workflows show extensive executable and workflow-level testing. | I did not inspect historical issue-tracking linkage for every discovered failure. | Preserve fail-closed security tests and keep coverage focused on security-critical paths. Reduces regression risk. | | `PW.9.1`-`PW.9.2` — secure settings by default | `OBSERVED` | `README.md` and design docs describe deny-by-default egress and credential-isolation defaults; product docs consistently position isolation and allowlisting as baseline behaviors. | Runtime deployment choices in consuming environments can still weaken defaults; that is outside repository-only proof. | Continue documenting safe defaults and test them in CI smoke flows. Reduces insecure deployment-by-default risk. | | `RV.1.1`-`RV.1.3` — identify and confirm vulnerabilities continuously | `OBSERVED` | `docs/security.md` defines disclosure intake; `codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, and `supply-chain-scan.yml` run on push/PR/schedule; Dependabot is enabled. | Private bug bounty, advisories, and security alert triage data were not accessible. | Keep scheduled detection and disclosure intake active; ensure alert owners are explicit outside the repo snapshot. Reduces time-to-detection. | | `RV.2.1`-`RV.2.2` — assess, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities | `PARTIAL` | Failing workflows on high/critical findings and coverage regressions show repository-level prioritization logic; release docs and issue references in design notes show remediation work is tracked in source history. | SLA, prioritization rubric, and exception governance are not repository-observable. | Document remediation ownership and exception handling where repository contributors can see it. Reduces inconsistent response. | | `RV.3.1`-`RV.3.4` — root-cause analysis and SDLC improvement | `PARTIAL` | `.github/workflows/shared/self-hosted-failure-modes.md` records root causes, fixes, and validation guidance for recurring security/operational defects; tests and docs accompany many mitigations. | Could not confirm the same discipline for every security vulnerability class. | Continue codifying root causes and regression tests for security-relevant incidents. Reduces repeat defects. |
Prioritized improvement backlog ### Promoted repository changes | Priority | Recommendation | SSDF mapping | Evidence | Risk rationale | Owner surface | Dependencies | Acceptance checks | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Publish and verify signed or attested integrity/provenance material for CLI release assets (`awf-*`, `awf-bundle.js`, `awf.tgz`) and make installer/setup paths fail closed on that verification. | `PS.2.1`, `PS.3.1`, `PS.3.2`, `PW.6.1`-`PW.6.2` | `.github/workflows/release.yml` signs and attests container images and selected enclave artifacts, but only generates `checksums.txt` for the CLI assets; `install.sh` and release docs trust the checksum file; `docs/image-verification.md` documents image verification only. | Release consumers get stronger tamper evidence for containers than for the CLI they install directly. A checksum file delivered on the same channel as the asset does not provide independent provenance or signer identity. | Maintainer / release engineering | Release workflow updates, installer/setup integration, docs, and tests | 1) release workflow publishes verifiable signatures or provenance for CLI assets; 2) `install.sh` and applicable setup paths validate them before install; 3) docs show user verification steps; 4) focused tests prove tampered asset/metadata paths fail closed. | ### Not promoted this run - Other SSDF areas were either already strong in repository evidence or depended mainly on non-repository organizational proof (training, branch protection governance, private alert handling, runner hardening, response SLAs).
Strengths worth preserving - Commit-pinned GitHub Actions across security-sensitive workflows. - Multiple independent detection layers: CodeQL, npm audit to SARIF, Dependabot, Grype/Grant supply-chain scanning, and coverage/test gates. - Strong container-release hygiene with cosign signatures and SBOM attestations. - Extensive design documentation for isolation, authentication, enclaves, and threat-model assumptions. - Dedicated CODEOWNERS ownership and security disclosure documentation.
Human-review questions 1. Are branch protection/rulesets enforcing the intended review and required-check policy on `main` and release branches? 2. Is there already an internal signing/provenance process for CLI release assets that is not reflected in public workflow/docs? If so, can public verification guidance be aligned to it? 3. How are vulnerability-remediation SLAs, exceptions, and secure-development training tracked outside the repository, and are they periodically reviewed against SSDF expectations? 4. Are CI runners and release environments segmented and monitored consistent with the repository’s documented isolation model?
